name: Institutional ORB + Brooks Box
tagline: Opening Range Breakout with confluence scoring and Al Brooks price action context
description: A complete opening-range trading system. It builds the opening range, classifies the day type (Coil, Breakout, Trading Range), then grades every breakout with a confluence score from A+ to C using gap analysis, VWAP positioning, relative volume, time-of-day quality, and ADR consumption. Brooks Box logic frames the session in Al Brooks price action context so you only take breakouts with institutional participation behind them.
features: Confluence scoring engine (0–8 points) graded A+ / A / B / C
Automatic day-type classification: COIL, BREAKOUT, TRADING RANGE
Initial Balance extensions with measured-move targets
Gap analysis: up gap, down gap, gap fill tracking
Relative volume gate — signals suppressed without volume confirmation
ADR consumption meter to avoid late-day chasing
Time-of-day quality filter (prime / neutral / caution windows)
Optional suppression of trading-range days and lunch chop

description: Linda Raschke's trading principles encoded into an objective bull/bear scoring engine. When a side reaches the minimum threshold with volume confirmation, the indicator prints a graded signal: from full trend entries to pullback continuations, failed-breakout fades, and exhaustion warnings.
features: Live Bull Score and Bear Score (0–12) with rule-by-rule checklist
Triple EMA stack analysis (9 / 20 / 50) with alignment states
Signal quality grading: STRONG, SOLID, MODERATE, WEAK
Six signal types covering trend, pullback, fade, and exhaustion setups
Volume confirmation gate on every signal
RSI and ATR context in the dashboard panel

name: Sire Trade Qualification
tagline: Eight-point pre-trade gate — only fires when institutional context lines up
description: A pre-trade qualification engine, not a signal generator. Every bar is run through eight institutional checks — EMA 20/50/200 trend stack, volume against its MA, proximity to prior swing levels, session timing, strong-bar confirmation, ATR-bounded stop distance, minimum R:R, and higher-timeframe context. A setup only qualifies when at least 6 of 8 pass. The live scorecard shows you exactly which checks failed in real time, so you can read context — not just signals. Designed to be paired with the Brooks Box framework on the same chart for the highest-conviction entries.

name: Sire Cockpit
tagline: All-in-one price-action HUD — structure, timing, bias and ICT zones on a single chart
description: A full chart command center that layers seven modules into one overlay so you can read structure, timing, bias and institutional zones at a glance. Market structure is mapped with automatic HH / HL / LH / LL pivots and self-extending support/resistance. A TD Sequential engine counts setups and prints 9s and 13s. A fast/slow EMA pair plus a higher-timeframe 200 EMA give trend bias. Inside-bar and IOI (inside-outside-inside) compression patterns are flagged, and a session bar-counter keeps you oriented inside the RTH window. The ICT layer draws Fair Value Gaps, Implied FVGs, Liquidity Voids, Volume Imbalances and true Gaps with full mitigation tracking. Standard FVG zones are detected on a selectable higher timeframe (30-minute by default) using only closed candles, so the zones are non-repainting and drawn cleanly on your execution chart. ICT zone engine adapted from open-source work by Vulnerable_human_x under the Mozilla Public License 2.0.
features: Auto market structure: HH / HL / LH / LL pivots with self-extending support & resistance
TD Sequential setup counter with 9 and 13 prints plus optional pulse trails
EMA stack (fast/slow) plus higher-timeframe 200 EMA with slope coloring
Multi-timeframe FVG detection — pick any timeframe, 30m default, non-repainting
Full ICT zone engine: FVG, Implied FVG, Liquidity Void, Volume Imbalance, true Gaps
Mitigation tracking with Engulf / Mitigate / Rebalance modes and live highlight on tag
Inside-bar coloring (on by default) and IOI compression pattern flags
Session bar-counter for RTH structure with configurable interval and hourly markers
On-chart SireMammat's Cockpit watermark with full position and styling control

name: GreenLight Pro Enhanced
tagline: Eight subsystems on one clean chart — L8/B8 momentum gated by EMA, volume, structure and a 0–4 confluence score
description: A streamlined multi-system trading suite that folds momentum signal generation, structural swing analysis, TD Sequential exhaustion, candlestick patterns and volume analysis into one clean overlay. The heart is the GreenLight Core: it counts consecutive momentum bars (L1–L8 / B1–B8) and only fires an L8/B8 PRO signal when six filters agree — EMA side, EMA slope, 0.75× ATR proximity, 1.2× volume, trending structure, and a configurable 0–4 confluence score. Around it sit Brooks' Gap 20 tracker, the 18-bar RTH opening-range box (Coil / BO / TR), TD Sequential, OO/II/IOI candle patterns, two-leg & 3-push wedge detection, and HH/HL/LH/LL swing structure with dynamic S/R. This Clean Edition strips the old PA-entry arrows, Always-In arrows, inside-bar breakout arrows and the duplicate slow EMA, leaving only high-conviction, actionable signals. Optimized for MNQ/MES futures; works on any instrument with volume.

howToUse: Open TradingView and go to Pine Editor (bottom panel).
Copy the full source from the file linked below and paste it into the editor.
Click "Add to chart". Use a 5-minute chart (primary) on MNQ/MES/NQ/ES; add a 15-minute for confirmation.
Let the opening range form, then read the State Table — if it shows CHOP (orange), stand aside; if TREND (green), proceed.
Take L8/B8 PRO labels scoring 3/4 or 4/4 in the direction of the structure; treat L4/B4 dots as a heads-up only.
Confirm with the dashboard (structure matches direction), TD Sequential (no opposing exhaustion) and swing structure, then use the R:R overlay's stop and target to manage the trade.
bestPractices: Trend only — L8/B8 fire just in UPTREND/DOWNTREND; in TRADING RANGE or CHOP the signals are suppressed, so don't force them.
Best window is the 10:00–11:30 ET morning session on above-average volume; the 11:30–13:30 lunch lull produces lower-probability signals.
Prioritize score 4/4 over 3/4, and weight setups where multiple systems agree (e.g. L8 PRO + UPTREND + HH/HL, or B8 PRO + TD Buy CD13 + Gap 20).
Respect the 18-bar box: COIL favors a patient breakout, BO favors trading with trend, TR favors fading the extremes.
A Countdown 13 or a 3-push wedge against your direction is a reason to tighten or wait — confirm exhaustion before countering a trend.

name: 2 Legged PB M2B/M2S
tagline: Two-legged pullback continuation entries at the 20 EMA—M2B in bull trends, M2S in bear trends
description: A trend-continuation setup based on the classic two-legged pullback described in Al Brooks price-action methodology. Instead of chasing an extended move, the indicator waits for price to correct in two distinct legs toward the 20 EMA, then looks for confirmation back in the direction of the established trend. M2B identifies a second-entry buy after a two-legged pullback in a bullish market; M2S identifies a second-entry sell after a two-legged rally in a bearish market. The setup is strongest when market structure, EMA slope, and signal-bar quality all agree.

20 EMA location and trend-direction confirmation
M2B second-entry long setups in bullish structure
M2S second-entry short setups in bearish structure
Signal-bar confirmation before an entry is armed
Defined entry, structural stop, and target framework
Designed for clear trends rather than trading ranges

Copy the full source linked below, paste it into the editor, and click “Add to chart.”
Confirm a clear trend first: higher highs and higher lows for M2B, or lower lows and lower highs for M2S.
Wait for two distinct pullback legs toward the 20 EMA—do not treat the first EMA test as the completed setup.
Require a credible signal bar that closes back toward the trend direction.

Manage risk from the second-leg extreme, scale at the prior swing, and never widen the original stop.
bestPractices: Strong Trend—trade M2B only with a rising 20 EMA and M2S only with a falling 20 EMA; skip a flat average.
Clear Two Legs—the A-B-C structure should be obvious without forcing the count.
EMA Confluence—the second leg should touch or approach the 20 EMA while the broader trend remains intact.
Signal-Bar Quality—prefer a strong rejection or trend bar; avoid weak dojis and overlapping congestion.
Room to Target—make sure the prior swing offers enough reward relative to the structural stop.
Trading Range Filter—M2B/M2S loses its edge when price repeatedly crosses a flat EMA.
News Filter—avoid initiating the setup within 30 minutes of FOMC, CPI, or NFP.

name: TD Sequential
tagline: Tom DeMark momentum-exhaustion system — Setup 9 and Countdown 13 for reversal detection
description: A momentum-exhaustion indicator developed by Tom DeMark in the 1990s, used by institutional desks worldwide. It works in two phases: Setup (1–9) counts consecutive directional bars relative to the close four bars earlier, and Countdown (1–13) confirms exhaustion. A completed Setup 9 is a caution flag; a Countdown 13 is the highest-conviction reversal signal in the system. Best used to call exhaustion at the end of an extended trend, never as a standalone.
features: Setup phase (1–9) flags potential trend exhaustion
Countdown phase (1–13) confirms the reversal zone
Recycling detection when a new setup interrupts the countdown
Most reliable on 15-minute and higher timeframes
Institutional-grade methodology used across major platforms

name: Sire FVG Setup Finder
tagline: ICT Fair Value Gaps with a full trade plan — auto entry, stop and target the moment price taps the imbalance
description: Most FVG indicators stop at drawing boxes. This one finishes the job. It detects every 3-candle imbalance (Fair Value Gap), filters out the noise with an ATR size gate, then waits for the moment that actually matters — price trading back into the gap. That tap is the setup. The instant it happens, the indicator prints a complete trade plan on your chart: entry at the gap edge, stop beyond the far edge with an ATR cushion, and a target set by your risk:reward. It then tracks the trade live and marks whether TP or SL got hit first — with a conservative SL-first rule on ambiguous bars, so it never flatters its own results. Written in Pine v6.
features: Bullish and bearish FVG detection (3-candle imbalance) with ATR minimum-size filter
Setup flag the moment price mitigates the gap — wick taps AND full pierces both count
Auto trade plan on every setup: Entry / SL / TP lines with price labels
Two entry modes (gap edge or touch-bar close) and two stop modes (gap far edge + buffer, or pure ATR)
Honest exit tracking — no same-bar instant exits, SL-first default when one bar hits both levels
Six alert conditions: gap formed (bull/bear), long entry, short entry, TP hit, SL hit

howToUse: Open TradingView and go to Pine Editor (bottom panel).
Copy the full source from the file linked below and paste it into the editor.
Click "Add to chart". Works 1m–4H; 5m–15m is the sweet spot for ES/NQ session trading.
Set Min gap size to 0.25–0.5× ATR — untouched, it will draw every micro-gap.
Wait for the Setup flag — the gap forming is context, the tap is the trade.
Set alerts to "Once per bar close" if you want confirmed signals only; intrabar taps fire live.
bestPractices: Trade with displacement — the best FVGs form on a strong impulse leg. A gap inside chop is a skip.
Direction filter — take longs only into bullish FVGs above HTF support, shorts into bearish FVGs below HTF resistance. Don't fade the daily.
Fresh gaps only — first tap is the trade. A gap that's been tapped is spent; the indicator enforces this for you.
No News — skip if FOMC, CPI, or NFP is within 30 minutes. Imbalances get run both ways.
It's a map, not a backtest — this is an indicator, not a strategy(). The TP/SL tracking is honest (SL-first, no same-bar exits) but it is not fill simulation. Size accordingly.

name: BPA Mixed v2
tagline: All-in-one intraday HUD — session levels, RTH structure, outside-bar toolkit, EMAs, TD Sequential, and body-gap tracking
description: A complete intraday price-action overlay combining session structure (open of day, prior day high/low, weekly/monthly levels), outside-bar trade management (entry levels, stop placement, risk targets), pattern detection (OO / II / IOI / H2 sequences), momentum analysis (three independently configurable EMAs), TD Sequential exhaustion counts, bar numbering through the RTH window, and automated body-gap zone tracking. Refactored from v1 with fixes for label leaks, session detection edge cases, forex scaling, and array mutation during iteration. Single source of truth for all patterns — OB toolkit plots support/resistance zones, measured-move targets, follow-through signals, and small-body arrows in one cohesive framework. Bars are colored by consecutive bull/bear strength or outside-bar type, giving instant visual feedback on momentum buildup.

Session Bar Counter: RTH bar numbering with configurable interval and hourly close markers
Body-Gap Zones: automated tracking of the last N bull/bear body gaps with live mitigation
Barbwire Detection: Doji-based compression + deep pullback zones for reversal confluence
Info Dashboard: average session range (ADR), current session range, gap size, scalp/swing/stop ranges, hourly ATR
Globex Tracking: optional pre-market high/low accumulation during non-RTH hours
Merged Bar Coloring: consecutive bull/bear bars, outside-bar type shading, inside-bar highlighting — all in one priority expression

howToUse: Open TradingView and go to Pine Editor (bottom panel).
Copy the full source from the file linked below and paste it into the editor.
Click 'Add to chart'. Use a 1m–15m intraday chart on ES/NQ/MES/MNQ.
Let the session open and wait for the first bars to populate the session levels (ood, hoy, loy).
Read the three EMAs for trend bias, then look for OB setup opportunities in that direction.
When an OB prints, the lines show your stop level (±1 tick) and risk target (measured-move distance).
Watch for H2 sequences (two OBs expanding in range) and II take-off patterns (compression breaks) for higher-conviction entries.
Use the bar counter to stay oriented in the RTH window; the info dashboard shows gap size and ADR for context.
Body gaps auto-update as price fills; use them as support/resistance reference points.
The info table calculates scalp / swing / stop ranges based on the session ADR — use these as R:R guides.
bestPractices: EMA stack alignment = trend bias. Trade OB setups in the direction the three EMAs favor.
H2 sequences (consecutive expanding OBs) are higher probability than single OB setups; wait for the pattern to complete.
Small-body arrows before an OB often mark the setup that's about to fire — they're early-warning dots, not signals by themselves.
Respect the info dashboard: if gap size is > 100% of ADR and the market has just opened, stands back — a gap-fill trade is likely in progress.
TD 13 landing in an unmitigated body-gap zone is high-probability confluence to take profits or reverse.
Use bar count to identify the time window: the 10–11:30 AM window is highest probability; 11:30–1:30 PM is often lunch chop.
OB Follow-Through arrows are confirmation, not entries. Enter on the setup (the OB itself), confirm with follow-through.
Outside-bar measured moves often run the full bar-height distance. The blue line shows the full projection; take partial profits at halfway.

name: LBR 3-10 Oscillator
tagline: Linda Raschke’s momentum oscillator for bias, acceleration, and exhaustion
description: The LBR 3-10 Oscillator is Linda Bradford Raschke’s compact momentum framework built from the difference between a 3-period and 10-period simple moving average. The fast line shows raw short-term momentum, the 16-period smoothing line acts as the slower signal, and their difference forms a histogram that reveals acceleration or deceleration. Use the zero line to frame directional bias, fast/slow crosses and histogram flips to detect momentum shifts, and pivot divergence to spot potential exhaustion. It is a context and timing tool—not a standalone buy-or-sell system.

Slow signal line: 16-period SMA of the fast line
Acceleration histogram: Fast − Slow

Fast/slow crossover signals for momentum shifts
Histogram color flips for early acceleration and deceleration reads
Pivot-based bullish and bearish divergence detection
Configurable source, lengths, pivot strength, and display controls

Copy the full source from the file linked below, paste it into the editor, and click “Add to chart.”
Start with the default 3 / 10 / 16 settings; they are the defining structure of the oscillator.
Use the fast line above zero as bullish momentum context and below zero as bearish momentum context.
Watch fast/slow crosses and histogram flips for changes in acceleration, then confirm with price structure.
Treat divergence as an exhaustion warning only after its pivot is confirmed—not as an automatic reversal entry.
bestPractices: Trade with structure: use the oscillator to confirm a breakout, pullback, or failed-breakout setup already visible in price.
Prefer bullish momentum signals above zero and bearish signals below zero; counter-bias signals require stronger confirmation.
Histogram flips often lead zero-line crosses, but they can whipsaw in ranges—check trend and nearby support or resistance.
Divergence is strongest after an extended move into a meaningful level and weakest inside ordinary chop.
Do not optimize away the 3 / 10 / 16 identity without testing; changing those lengths produces a different momentum tool.
Use alerts as prompts to review context, never as instructions to enter automatically.

name: Sire Order Blocks
tagline: Structure-confirmed order blocks with displacement filtering, FVG confluence, and mitigation tracking
description: Sire Order Blocks identifies institutional-style supply and demand zones only after price confirms a break of structure. A bullish order block is the last bearish candle before an ATR-qualified displacement move closes above a confirmed swing high; a bearish order block is the last bullish candle before price closes below a confirmed swing low. Optional Fair Value Gap confluence keeps only zones whose impulse leg contains an imbalance. Every zone then extends forward, changes appearance when mitigated, and is removed when price closes through its far side. The result is a selective structure map designed to distinguish meaningful order blocks from every ordinary opposing candle.
features: Bullish and bearish order-block detection confirmed by Break of Structure (BOS)
Pivot-based swing structure with configurable confirmation strength
ATR displacement filter suppresses weak or random structure breaks
Optional Fair Value Gap confluence within the displacement leg
Full-wick or candle-body zone construction
Live mitigation tracking by wick touch or closing price
Automatic invalidation when price closes through the far side
Configurable zone limits, colors, labels, and mitigated-zone visibility

Begin with Require FVG enabled and the 1.5× ATR displacement filter to focus on cleaner institutional impulses.
Read +OB zones as potential demand and −OB zones as potential supply, but wait for price to revisit the zone.
Use the first mitigation as the primary decision point; combine it with trend, session context, and a price-action trigger.
Place invalidation beyond the far side of the zone and size the trade from that structural risk—not from a fixed contract count.
If too few zones appear, reduce the displacement multiplier or disable FVG confluence; if the chart is noisy, do the opposite.
bestPractices: Fresh zones matter most: the first return generally carries more information than repeated tests.
Trade with higher-timeframe direction; bullish blocks in an uptrend and bearish blocks in a downtrend have better context.
Prioritize OB • FVG zones created by decisive displacement through an obvious swing level.
A zone is context, not an entry signal—require rejection, a lower-timeframe structure shift, or another defined trigger.
Use close-based mitigation for stricter confirmation and wick-touch mitigation for earlier, more sensitive tracking.
Do not keep trusting a block after price closes through its far side; the script removes invalidated zones automatically.
Avoid treating every displayed block equally around major news or low-liquidity periods.

name: Sire Adaptive Kalman Filter Pro
tagline: Adaptive order-flow pressure combining CVD, VWAP, Initial Balance, and trend-day confirmation
description: A Quantower-native pressure oscillator built around an adaptive Kalman filter. Instead of relying only on price change, its measurement model blends session cumulative volume delta, ATR-normalized location relative to session VWAP, position versus the Initial Balance, and confirmed trend-day expansion. The indicator automatically selects its data mode on every update: it displays ORDER FLOW when valid Quantower Volume Analysis delta is available, switches to PRICE FALLBACK when it is unavailable and fallback is enabled, or supplies a neutral measurement when fallback is disabled. The filter becomes more conservative during elevated volatility.

Reassess bias when price accepts back through the weekly open or IB midpoint.
bestPractices: Week-start timestamps depend on the data connection and instrument session template.
Acceptance requires time and trade beyond a level; a wick alone is not confirmation.
Extensions work best as planning references and scale-out zones.
Prior-week levels can remain relevant even after the current IB expands.
